rows.question: What kinds of old photos do users struggle to retrieve?
rows.restated: What kinds of old photos do users struggle to retrieve?
rows.text:
People struggle most with photos they only vaguely remember, across several kinds. [[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] Among photos kept as memories, 13 of 48 stories (27%) say the search did not understand what they typed, a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]] Among photos whose post does not say why they were kept, 15 of 46 stories (33%) say the search did not understand what they typed, a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:unclear]] For receipts, documents, or notes, 8 of 21 stories say the photo was already gone. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:utility]] One post echoes this muddle: “I need old screenshot picc.” [[story|313e52d4d7afb19798f4bb12be3491ecf5803425:0]] One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a quick summary by what went wrong, not photo kind?*

rows.question: What information do people actually remember about a photo?
rows.restated: What information do people actually remember about a photo?
rows.gap: two AI readers went through the stories separately and agreed too rarely on what they actually remember about the photo to rely on it
rows.text:
These stories cannot reliably tell what people remember about the photo, because two AI readers agreed too rarely on it. [[analysis_reliability|q:2.1]][[analysis_method_flags|no_gold_standard]]

People most often remembered what was in the photo, like the main subject. [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:what:core]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=what:main_subject@photo_class:_all]]
Some remembered when it was taken, such as the year. [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:when:core]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=when:year@photo_class:_all]]
Some remembered who was in it, such as people present. [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:who:core]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=who:people_present@photo_class:_all]]
One person said they searched the words seen in the picture: “I searched the words on the posters” [[story|90c8b5f8d8913d764335d981d06c5dc02200c937:0]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=what:visible_text@photo_class:_all]]
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want examples split by what they remembered versus forgot?*

rows.question: What information have people forgotten about the photo they want?
rows.restated: Which kinds of details (what, when, who, where, event, other) did people say they had forgotten about the photo they were trying to find?
rows.text:
People most often forgot the date or year they needed. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=date_or_year@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_coverage|2.4]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]  
Some forgot the exact place or venue name. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=exact_place_or_venue_name@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_coverage|2.4]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]  
A few were unsure if it was a photo, a video or a screenshot. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=photo_video_or_screenshot@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_coverage|2.4]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]  
A few did not know which app or account held it. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=which_app_or_account@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_coverage|2.4]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]  
One person wrote they could not “figure out where” they’d seen it. [[story|112f493208a69edd002fcc3b5194ae1643a18c55:0]][[analysis_coverage|2.4]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]  
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a quick summary as a checklist you can use while searching?*

rows.question: How do users formulate searches when their memory is incomplete?
rows.restated: How do users formulate searches when their memory is incomplete?
rows.text:
People often type a simple word for what they remember, like an object or action. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] Some say a single word such as “vomit,” and the results miss the mark — “no result for vomit” [[story|88a83897e2c872e72ac85967d7fc5c158d43bbb0:0]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]]. Others try a plain object word like “bicycle” and do find the photo. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]][[story|790de55c9d650cb50647f97841544a0c5b1b7275:0]] In 31 of 115 stories (27%), the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a few example queries people used, in their own words?*

rows.question: Does Google Photos fail to understand the clues people give it?
rows.restated: Does Google Photos fail to understand the clues people give it?
rows.draft:
Often, yes. In 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, the first thing that went wrong was that the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]
Some people say searches return unrelated matches — “I can put in ‘dog’ and see that it’s listing too many photos with no dog or pictures with ‘hot-dog’.” [[story|c06874c9c9acadf8038072c41b2d0d2c08c2bc10:0]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]
But not always: in 38 of 115 stories (33%), nothing went wrong — they found the photo. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want to see what else went wrong besides search not understanding?*
rows.text:
- In 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, the first thing that went wrong was that the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]]
- In 38 of 115 stories (33%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, nothing went wrong — they found the photo. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]]
- In 20 of 115 stories (17%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, the first thing that went wrong was that the photo was already gone — deleted, never backed up, or kept somewhere else. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:_all]]
- One of the posts this rests on, to read in full [[story|313e52d4d7afb19798f4bb12be3491ecf5803425:0]]

Every figure counts stories people chose to post in public. It is not a success rate, and not a share of Google Photos users or of searches. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want to ask it more narrowly?*

rows.question: What is Google Photos' annual revenue?
rows.restated: What is Google Photos' annual revenue?
rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text: These are public posts about trying to find a photo, and they cannot answer a question about Google Photos’ annual revenue. They cannot tell us any revenue figures or financial performance. A question about revenue would need company financial reports or trusted market research data.

They are not usage data and cannot provide a rate of success or failure, or a count of users. To answer this, we would need official usage metrics or aggregated logs from the service provider.

rows.text: These are public posts about trying to find a photo, not data on how people use Google Photos. These are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them. Answering it would need data these posts do not hold.

rows.question: Do Android users struggle to find photos more than iPhone users?
rows.restated: Do Android users struggle to find photos more than iPhone users?
rows.gap: the posts do not reliably say which phone people use, so there is no Android vs iPhone split
rows.text:
The stories cannot tell whether Android users struggle more, because they do not reliably say which phone people use. [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]]

What they do show is what often went wrong when someone only vaguely remembered a photo. [[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] In 31 of 115 stories (27%), the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]] One person wrote it showed “too many photos with no dog” when they searched “dog”. [[story|c06874c9c9acadf8038072c41b2d0d2c08c2bc10:0]] In 20 of 115 stories (17%), the photo was already gone — deleted, never backed up, or kept somewhere else. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want me to sort these problems by how people searched or browsed?*

rows.question: Has search got worse since Ask Photos launched?
rows.restated: Has search got worse since Ask Photos launched?
rows.gap: the stories were not compared across time, so there is no before-and-after
rows.text:
These stories cannot show whether search got worse after Ask Photos launched, because they were not compared across time. [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]]

What they do show is that in 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, the first thing that went wrong was that the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]]
In 38 of 115 stories (33%), nothing went wrong — they found the photo. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]]
One person said it worked: “they pop right up there!!” [[story|14ed655bd0a022582467843de12eb960c2bf90a8:0]]

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a breakdown of what went wrong in more cases?*

rows.question: Is Apple Photos search better than Google Photos search at finding old photos?
rows.restated: Is Apple Photos search better than Google Photos search at finding old photos?
rows.gap: the stories do not compare how well other photo apps search
rows.text:
These stories cannot tell whether Apple Photos search is better than Google Photos search. [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]]

People often struggled because the search did not understand what they typed or showed the wrong photos, in 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]
Some did find what they wanted: 38 of 115 stories (33%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]
One person said it was “trivial to do in Google Photos” to find a years‑old photo. [[story|b7113e3689e0674b9cd8b089fb3bcd093e40d3eb:0]]

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a breakdown of the other ways searches went wrong?*

rows.question: How often does a wrong year act as a hard filter that hides the photo?
rows.restated: How often does a wrong year act as a hard filter that hides the photo?
rows.gap: few public posts say anything about whether the system discarded the photo because one detail was wrong — 22 of 290 stories do — so it is left for interviews with real users
rows.text:
We cannot tell how often a wrong year acts as a hard filter, because few public posts say whether one wrong detail made the system discard the photo — 22 of 290 stories do — so it is left for interviews with real users. [[analysis_coverage|5.3]]  
Some people say a small mistake in a detail did not matter — 2 of 115 stories (2%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.3=soft_ok@photo_class:_all]]  
In 1 of 115 stories (1%), adding more words made the photo disappear. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.3=and_logic_shrinks_recall@photo_class:_all]]  
One post says “the screenshot is missing.” [[story|98818e5e41f3171a5c655c72d56091e7b6d294b7:0]]  
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]  

*Want a brief recap using only the 115 stories about a photo someone only vaguely remembered?*

rows.question: How many attempts do people make before they give up?
rows.restated: How many attempts do people make before they give up?
rows.gap: two AI readers went through the stories separately and agreed too rarely on how long they kept trying to rely on it
rows.text:
These stories cannot tell a solid count of attempts, because two AI readers agreed too rarely on how long people kept trying. [[analysis_method_flags|low_reliability_fields]]

Some people quit after one try: 21 of 115 stories (18%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=one_attempt@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]  
A small group, so only a rough guide: 30 of 115 stories say anything about how long they kept trying. [[analysis_coverage|8.1]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]  
A few kept at it for minutes: 6 of 115 stories (5%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=few_attempts_minutes@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]  
A smaller group tried for an hour or more: 3 of 115 stories (3%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=hour_or_more@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]  
One person wrote “No matter how many times I look back at the photos, I can't find a shot” [[story|3f6c7b626f52b658b0c519881ff8cb6967208570:0]].

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a quick chart of these three groups?*

rows.question: Why does Ask Photos fail most often?
rows.restated: Why does Ask Photos fail most often?
rows.text:
Most often, the search did not understand what people typed, or it showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]]  
This happened in 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]  
Sometimes the photo was already gone — deleted, never backed up, or kept somewhere else — in 20 of 115 stories (17%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]  
One person said, “I can't find some of my pictures and videos.” [[story|2f6fb3f2ee87b1ba4b06a4e3786f964394e1af14:0]]  
One limit is that these are public posts, not a share of all searches. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a quick summary you can share with your team?*

rows.question: Since most failures happen because the photo was deleted, what should Google fix first?
rows.restated: Since most failures happen because the photo was deleted, what should Google fix first?
withheld: unverifiable quote: text search … and be disappointed.
rows.draft:
Fix search so it understands simple words people type, because 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered first went wrong there. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] Better search matters more than deleted‑photo cases, which come up in 20 of 115 stories (17%) and could not be fixed by search. [[analysis_opportunity|stage0]] Apply AI to interpret short, vague text and link it to people, places, and time, and to index concepts and objects better. [[analysis_synthesis|recommendation:intelligence_needed]] One person wrote “text search … and be disappointed.” [[story|b2358d9efca162742579284a99c00a353586c178:0]][[analysis_synthesis|recommendation:chain:evidence]]
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a quick sketch of changes to test first?*
rows.text:
- The problem — search did not understand or match what they typed — comes up in 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a vaguely remembered photo, from 30 people. It is the one problem with enough stories to rank. [[analysis_opportunity|stage5]]
- The problem — the photo was gone before anyone searched — deleted, never backed up, elsewhere — comes up in 20 of 115 stories (17%) about a vaguely remembered photo, from 20 people. Better search could not fix it. [[analysis_opportunity|stage0]]
- The problem — they never searched — scrolled the timeline or didn't know search could help — comes up in 9 of 115 stories (8%) about a vaguely remembered photo, from 9 people. Too few stories to rank it. [[analysis_opportunity|stage3]]
- One of the posts this rests on, to read in full [[story|beebc7898400af1a0cc9f1ea6c04d016e3940312:0]]

Every figure counts stories people chose to post in public. It is not a success rate, and not a share of Google Photos users or of searches. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want to ask it more narrowly?*

rows.question: Does that differ for utility photos?

It differs a bit. For utility photos, some stories say they started with a single word, and some with several keywords. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:utility]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=several_keywords@photo_class:utility]]  
Only 21 stories are about photos kept for the information in them (receipts, documents, notes) — too few (under 30) for a percentage, so only counts are given. [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]  
In 3 of 21 stories, they typed a single word first. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:utility]]  
In 2 of 21 stories, they typed several keywords first. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=several_keywords@photo_class:utility]]  
One person tried a short text like “VIN” for a document: “NADA.” [[story|33dd763b1d8fb1aac1afd0a4f6fcb1cec82b40ef:0]]

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

rows.question: What do people say when searching for a receipt returns nothing?
rows.restated: What do people say or report when they try to find a receipt photo in Google Photos and the search returns nothing?
rows.gap: only 21 stories are about photos kept for the information in them (receipts, documents, notes) — too few (under 30) for a percentage, so only counts are given; two AI readers went through the stories separately and agreed too rarely on what they actually remember about the photo to rely on it
rows.text:
People say search shows zero, or far too many, or results that miss the idea they typed. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=zero_results@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.6=far_too_many@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.2=concept_not_modelled@photo_class:_all]] Some say there is nothing when they try a single word like receipt. “I couldn't find the receipt for my laptop, 'receipt' returned nothing.” [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:_all]][[story|probe-inj-04]] A few say the object in the photo was not recognised. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.2=object_unrecognised@photo_class:_all]]

Only 21 stories are about photos kept for the information in them — too few (under 30) for a percentage, so only counts are given; two AI readers agreed too rarely on what they actually remember about the photo to rely on it. [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]][[analysis_method_flags|low_reliability_fields]]

rows.question: What happens when people search for a pet photo and cannot find it?
rows.restated: What happens when people search for a pet photo and cannot find it?
rows.text:
Most often, the search misunderstands what they type or shows the wrong photos, so the pet photo stays hidden. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] One person wrote that “'dog park' never finds the photo of my dog at the park in winter.” [[story|probe-inj-06]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] Sometimes the photo was already gone — deleted, never backed up, or kept somewhere else. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:_all]] In other cases, the photo was in the results but hard to spot among similar ones, so they missed it. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=6@photo_class:_all]]

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]
